design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (microsoft_365_subscriptions), round 2
Draw: draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4,6,4]; reduction credit 4, late charge 6, payment arrangement 4.
Why a good test: the client asks only to arrange and part-pay a past-due Microsoft 365 invoice. The agent must read that the first instalment waits on the month's late charge and that the late charge waits on every in-window reduction carrying its credit; find in the ledger that the 2026-08-12 reduction has none; post it, assess October's charge on the corrected balance, then compute the first instalment, each with factors read from the licensing ledger and the ClearPath (managed) agreement and ledger.
Scope: task 0 claims licensing_ext_reduction_credit, licensing_ext_late_charge, licensing_ext_payment_arrangement and tools post_reduction_credit_23f8ed2c, assess_late_charge_e02563fc, pay_arrangement_instalment_a0d5f2e9 (user); task 1 keeps the admin fee, seat partial-cycle charge and window cancellation (disjoint).
Problem tree: root licensing_ext_payment_arrangement (user) <- licensing_ext_late_charge (value_input month_late; "The first instalment of a payment arrangement is not set until the late charge owed for the current month on the subscription's past-due cycle invoice stands on the billing ledger.") <- licensing_ext_reduction_credit (value_input past_due_balance; "The late charge on a cycle invoice is fixed only after the subscription's latest in-window reduction carries its reduction credit line on the billing ledger."). Both state form; only the late-charge write books late-charge rows and only the reduction-credit write books in_window_reduction credits (the cancellation books cancellation refunds). Directions: affirmative for the late charge ("fixed only after"), negated for the instalment ("not set until").
Unmet at frozen_time: no credit carries 435011cd-2e74-4e65-9cf5-25ddb5fbf8c2; no 2026-10 late charge. Deletion sensitivity (actual runs): skip credit -> late charge 22.58 (gold 21.66); skip late charge -> instalment 796.30 (gold 819.68).
Base-invariant card: refund credits — licensing_cancellation_window (the reduction met its 168-hour window: 64.5 h after the window opened 2026-08-10 00:00; overwrite scoped to whole-term cycles, sibling cancellation named, every in-window credit credited to the invoice that billed its cycle). Late fee and payment — licensing_billing_and_collections (due 2026-09-09, grace ends 2026-09-19, assessable 2026-10-01; card limit 10,000.00 >= 4,050.00; arrangements carry no fee). Late-fee overwrite scoped to annual cycle invoices.
Business-object card: subscription f13ccdff-f09d-49d8-a426-334028e1fa74; INV-024118 (cycle 2026-08-10) the only open invoice: cycle charge 4,050.00, payment 400.00, the new credit and late charge; INV-021077 / INV-022314 settled; the 2024 reduction credited by f45f55ce-d049-4872-9ae9-f3a09f03c8e7.
Factor card (expected / all-baseline; per-factor baseline figure):
RC 880.25 / 780.56: early_release_anchor [875.70], clearpath_change_fee [855.25], posting_delay_goodwill [830.25], review_miss_goodwill [860.00]. Near-miss: the older 2024 reduction (purchase window, credited).
LC 21.66 / 41.55: courtesy_rate [25.71], relationship_minimum [17.14], first_period_accrual [29.53], master_account_escalation [17.32], good_faith_relief [28.87], invoice_size_scale [24.06]. Near-misses: 2025-10-01 licensing late charge exactly 12 whole months back; ClearPath late fee 2025-09-01 thirteen months back.
PY 819.68 / 930.47: instalment_count [1338.55], down_payment_share [598.69], month_late_treatment [802.53], front_loading [715.90].
Cross-difficulty: managed. ClearPath Standard agreement 7a4d07a8-817a-499d-a2bb-f6a827f67d2c: initial 36-month term at 124.00 less 4% = 119.04; each 12-month renewal prices min(expiring x 1.05, 124.00 less 0%) = 124.00 (managed_renewal_and_uplift), so seat_rate_usd 124.00 after 5 renewals; contracted_seats = seat_count = 21 (no change since the 2026-04-08 renewal). managed_seat_changes: the 21-seat go-live baseline (no change since), reproducing seat_count. managed_billing (round 3, complete for 2025-07..2026-10): ClearPath history seeded from signing (round 9): ClearPath Standard signed 2024-03-11 for 21 seats on a 12-month term at the 124.00 list (no 12-month discount), onboarding fee 21 x 60.00 = 1,260.00 raised to the 1,750.00 minimum (no waiver below 36 months) and paid 2024-03-13, go-live 2024-04-08 with the 21-seat baseline, prorated 124.00 x 21 x 23/30 = 1,996.40 on the 2024-05-01 invoice. Renewals under the published automatic-renewal schedule: 2025-04-08 (first, 12-month expiring term, full 5% cap) = the lower of 130.20 and 124.00, less 0.5% (5 tickets against 21 seats, no late fee, no credit, no seat growth in 2024-04-08..2025-04-07) = 123.38; 2026-04-08 (second) = the lower of 129.55 and 124.00, net 0 (2 late fees +0.5, 6 tickets -0.5) = 124.00; renewal_count 2. Monthly fees, each posted on the 1st with no credit (no Business Premium, Sentinel or Continuum; fewer than 40 seats): 2,604.00 for 2024-05..2025-04, 2,590.98 for 2025-05..2026-04, 2,604.00 for 2026-05..2026-10, each paid the same day by card autopay except the 2025-07 and 2026-02 invoices, assessed under the published late-fee schedule: 2025-09-01 = (1.0% x 1,000 + 0.5% x 1,590.98, 10 payments in the 12 months) less 10% = 16.16, 2026-04-01 = (1.5% x 1,000 + 0.75% x 1,590.98, a late fee in the window) less 10% = 24.24, minimum 10.00 (12-23 months live); paid by ACH 2,607.14 and 2,615.22; balance 0.00. Every look-back of every priced ClearPath row falls inside the seeded history (signing onward).
Multi-source factors: courtesy_rate (licensing late-charge count AND renewal count), review_miss_goodwill (renewal window AND ClearPath vCIO reviews), month_late_treatment (licensing late charge AND ClearPath tier). instalment_count reads one agreement and is not counted as multi-source.
Round-5 changes: the front-loading sentence now defines its excluded window itself (late charges posted less than one whole month before the arrangement); the late charge left out for a dedicated account manager simply stays on the invoice outside the arrangement; figures unchanged. Round-4 changes: the instalment count's 'owes nothing' now includes a credit balance (compute owed <= 0); figures unchanged. Round-10 changes: the change-fee cap of half the prorated amount is stated in the standard method (baseline) rather than the combination order; no figure moves. Round-9 changes: ClearPath history seeded from signing so every look-back is covered (go-live 2024-04-08; late fee 2025-09-01 now 16.16 at 1.0%); the reduction credit's change fee never takes more than half the prorated amount, so every reduction carries a positive credit line; figures unchanged. Round-8 changes: ClearPath rates and every ClearPath row repriced under the published renewal and fee schedules (123.38 then 124.00); the late-charge prerequisite waits on the latest in-window reduction's credit line, which the credit rule posts even at 0.00. Figures unchanged. Round-7 changes: ClearPath late fees repriced under the published ClearPath late-fee schedule (20.27, 24.33) with their payments; the client is located by phone; the reduction credit never falls below 0.00; the late charge's prerequisite waits on the latest in-window reduction (the one the credit rule prices). Figures unchanged. Round-3 changes: the ClearPath ledger completed (every monthly fee of the window and its payment, the seat ledger baseline; gold reads the seat ledger), all figures unchanged. Round-2 changes: assembly sentences generic (A3); down payment taken from the arrangement balance, the month's late charge handled as set-aside amounts (A5); the setup fee removed (an arrangement carries no fee) and front_loading added so the terminal ledger equals the rule; early_release_anchor tier 2 now reverses the source seat addition's billed charge in proportion (A6); credits are credited to the invoice that billed their cycle and the tool takes the cycle start; ClearPath seeds repriced at 124.00.
Persona: Renata volunteers the goal and why it slipped; phone/PIN, invoice and subscription only when asked; she runs the payment herself; if told something must be fixed first she says go ahead; she never states a figure.
Standard solution: locate -> verify (phone + PIN) -> read subscriptions, license changes, billing, ClearPath agreement and billing -> credit 880.25 on INV-024118 (cycle 2026-08-10) -> late charge 21.66 -> hand over; client pays 819.68.
Verification: scratch builder replays gold with the real tools and evaluates every compute through check_compute.build_env/eval_compute at handling time; outputs equal computations[].expected.
Traps: late charge before the credit (22.58); crediting from the reduction date (standard 780.56); counting the 2025-10-01 charge in the 12-month window; spreading the late charge; three instalments.
Draft recomputation from visible context reproduces the same writes; no stage fact is a status registration.
user_scenario: You are Renata Esquivel, operations manager and the authorized contact for Fenwick Hale Wealth Partners, LLC, a small wealth advisory practice in Raleigh. You are calling Stratton Bay's client services desk on your own initiative, a little embarrassed and keen to get it sorted in one call. You open by saying: "Hi, this is Renata Esquivel from Fenwick Hale Wealth Partners. We got a past-due notice on our Microsoft 365 E3 subscription - the annual one. Our bookkeeper left in August and that invoice slipped through. We can't clear it all in one go this month, so I'd like to set up a payment arrangement and pay the first part today by card." You speak plainly and you do not know how Stratton Bay calculates anything. You only give identity details when the agent asks for them: your registered phone number is 9195550231 and the support PIN is 248613; you offer both together if asked to verify, and you do not volunteer the EIN or anything else. If the agent asks which invoice the notice is about, you read it off the letter: INV-024118. If asked which subscription, it is the Microsoft 365 E3 one billed once a year. If asked how many instalments you want or how much to pay today, you say you have no preference and will go with whatever Stratton Bay's arrangement terms set, and that you just want to know the amount due today. You will pay today's instalment yourself on the company card; you do not want the agent to take card details over the phone. Only when the agent tells you the amount of today's instalment and hands you the payment step do you run it once, with the subscription reference, the invoice number and the amount exactly as the agent gives them, and then read back the confirmation you receive. If the agent says something else on the account has to be put right before the arrangement can be set, you say "Fine, go ahead and do whatever is needed" and wait for the instalment amount. If an amount sounds off to you, you only say it is not what you expected and ask the agent to check it against the records; you never suggest a figure. Once the payment is confirmed you thank the agent and end the call.
